I can only speak for the single player experience here, but even ignoring the predatory microtransactions; this game is bad.

Optimisation is abysmal. Why is this game using 100% of my gpu? and why is it stuttering through menus? 9070xt, 9800x3d. 64gb 6000mhz ram.

The commentary is some of the worst I've experienced in a game. Roll a monster putt to within 5ft? "They'll be disappointed with that". 20 shots clear of your rival going into the final day of a tourney? "Really not sure which way this one is gonna go!". Tap in a birdie? "We'll put this hole behind us and move on". And if you play multiple rounds they use the same canned lines at the same points on each hole, it's insufferable.

The personalisation option are a joke; Cobra offers more choices of hat than they do clubs. And even the clubs they do have in are out of date; why offer 2023 models in 2k25? Then there's the sponsors - super simple (actually annoyingly so) to get, painful to complete (after 30 hours on MyCareer, placing 1st or 2nd in every comp, I've not completed a sponsor pass yet).

And lastly the actual golf experience is counter-intuitive and lazy. Want to know what the wind is doing? Too bad. Fancy a full round? Dig through the menus to find out how, otherwise the AI will decide how many holes you play (why on earth is that an option btw?).
Great game. Sounds and visuals are amazing compared to 2k23. In my opinion they are going in the right direction with the changes they made. It can be tough but it feels like its how it should be.
They updated the game after early access so the currency you earn in game (to but new clubs/clothes etc) is now also paid and takes a lot longer to gain.

Not a huge update over 2k23, but an improvement all the same. Online matchmaking still needs a lot more options as you're confined to the same options as before. The new quests mode is quite interesting and fun, should appeal to fans of mario golf and hot shots/everybody's golf, with rings and landing zones and arches. HUGE assortment of new and very faithfully recreated courses. Audio good, with perfect shots having a unique sound to them, along with improved crowd murmur and atmospherics. The menu music doesn't sound like something from a golf game though, and the announcers are identical to the old ones save for new stories and a few added phrases that sound like they were from the same awful mid-boosted session the rest were from. Overall, if you like golf games, and want a AAA title with real names/courses/products, this is the one to play.

It's egregious how poorly this game runs considering how much money they expect to make from microtransactions. The transitions become unbearable after a while, making the grind to earn in-game currency even more frustrating.

This company is vile. Their greed and disrespect of a loyal community is on full display in this title. People paid for the game and, in a lot of cases, pre-purchased the game in order to play early. They reaped good reviews and tricked everyone with how the leveling systems would work. Then, the day before the full launch, they completely overhauled the leveling system, turning it into an entirely different experience.

If you do not have several hours a day to play this game, your leveling process will be a slog and frustrating. Why??? Because in order to perform well on the course, your player needs to upgrade the attributes that "forgive" the more difficult elements involved in the new swing mechanics. The "overhaul" made this so that the most practical way to level up your character is to spend real $$$ on in-game currency. This is AFTER you've already spent probably close to $100 on the game itself. This is an absolute joke and a disgrace to gaming.

It's $70, but it is 1 of maybe 2 options you have to play golf on pc these days. It's as competitive as you want, and as technical as you want. Online players can bypass the grind with their wallet and be OVR 99 but that doesn't guarantee a win by any means.

PGA TOUR 2K25 - ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I never thought I would own a golf game, but PGA TOUR 2K25 has been a genuinely fun surprise. It is the first golf game I have ever owned, and recently I have been enjoying it more than expected.

For anyone looking for a fun sports game that is different from the usual choices, this is an easy one to recommend. It has made a great first impression, especially as my introduction to golf games.

It feels like they got a nice following from 2k 23 which was made for the players. 2k 25 was made with some cooperate design to milk money out of everyone. The physics, green speed, ball bouncing off angled fairway are out of wack and I feel like it's intentional to encourage you to spend money on their stupid Virtual Credit gimmick. It does look better than 23, but I feel like I'm in a foreign flee market being grabbed from all sides to spend extra money on f'n everything. Trash. My first and only review because out of principle I wanted people to know.
IF YOU LIKE GOLF, OR MAYBE YOU LOVE GOLF, THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU!

Pros: Swing mechanics great good for driver, irons, and full wedges. The game can be challenging if you put it on higher swing difficulty and I think makes it very fun to not always win. I like that you can quickly play rounds and I like the dynamic rounds (for the most part as I feel like it chooses the same holes always for some reason).

Cons: I 100% think there are far more cons unfortunately then pros. The overall production value outside of gameplay I subpar to put nicely. The announcing and dialogue is honestly unbearable. The commentary a lot of times does not match to what is happening on the course. The graphics are really quite poor. I thought it was my monitor, but then I decided to boot up EA, and the game is night and day better on production value front from commentary and graphics. As a golfer who watches and plays a lot, this part of the game really pulls me out of immersion. And lastly, the pay to win and the ridiculous speed at which you can earn VC is insane. I really was hoping this game would pull me back to a golf game, but I actually prefer EA over this, and I did not even play EA very long.

The only reason I would recommend buying this game is if you have a group of friends to play with or locally, only then the game can be fun, but at this price point, I dont see many groups buying multiple copies of it...

Pros: 
Looks fantastic graphically. Courses look similar to their respective real-world courses.
Ball physics are fine. Occasionally glitches such as a ball putt in the hole appears back on the green.
Good player customisation however the female character models are all overweight even on the skinniest setting.

Cons:
Menus are slow to load. I have never seen a menu system this bad in over 40 years of gaming since the 1980s. It makes the game tedious between rounds
User data stored in the cloud. No access to it when you have no internet access.
PvP mode does not seem to link players of similar skill level.
Bizarre non-intuitive levelling of clubs and equipment.
Swing glitches on every round I play. Appears like lag spikes.
Now can't access the game servers as they are down for me. Webiste syas they are up.
This list is not exhuastive. There are many othe rproblems.

I would not recommend this game, not even when on special.

PGA Tour 2K25 is a great game overall. The swing stick does come with a pretty steep learning curve, so expect to put in some time before you really get the hang of it. Building up your stats and upgrading your clubs is key if you want an edge on the course, and it's easy to lose track of time grinding and improving your game. If you're looking for a fun, competitive experience—especially playing duos with your boys—this one’s definitely worth checking out.

Absolutely love this game but the cheating in Ranked Matchmaking has been an absolute joke lately. I consider myself a decent player at this game (have gotten to Condor) and have at stages had my ranking dropped so far down due to playing a cheater every say 3/5 games. When it's their turn, you can tell straight away if they cheat, they barely aim, hit and put it in the perfect spot every time, all sped up. Same with approach shots and especially putts. Could be a putt with 30ft of break downhill and they take no time over it, putt and just speed the shot up and it's in. The fact that there is no way to report these players either is actually laughable. Don't even get me started with Online Societies. Cheaters going around 4 rounds -80 and -90 under. Clearly 2k could care less about it either. I would recommend this game if you want to play career mode. But don't if you want to play online, the cheaters are ruining it for everyone.

If I want to pay to lighten my bank account unnecessarily I will play real golf instead.....which I did today.

I mean, it's _fine_, definitely going to keep playing it. But it's not perfect. A couple gripes: the UI and animations are so agonizingly slow and painful. Just getting through myCareer after a round takes 5 minutes, every time you answer an email you have to watch the stupid animation again. It's so annoying! Another big thing I really am bummed about is there's no chill "let me play cool courses without fans or commentators" mode (edit: actually, quick play local lobby with community courses can get you this, which is cool! Old part of my review:). It's all competitive golf. That's really a damn shame. I was hoping I'd be able to just relax and play some rounds for fun but, no, it's all hyper competitive nonstop action with fans screaming and commentators judging every little shot. Got dang let a man just play some relaxing games of golf! Also beyond that the default mode is really easy. I'm just making great shot after great shot and it almost always sets me up to make a perfect shot. I need to play with the difficulty a bit because it feels like it's just handing me good holes and then it just comes down to putting.

tldr.text: Mixed (69%): players praise the gameplay and combat, while the price and monetization draw the most complaints.
Stutter, lag and bugs also come up often in reviews.

details.text: Players who review in their first couple of hours are far less positive, with only 21% positive, than those who have played longer.
Recent reviews are about as positive as the overall score, at 71%, so the mood has not shifted lately.
